home.whyTitle: Writing in French shouldn't cost a subscription.
home.whyBody: The good narrative-structure tools are English-speaking and paid. Atlas Narratif started from a simple observation: there was no free French equivalent that respects what you write. No advertising trackers, no AI training on your text, and an export of your data whenever you want. The tool handles structure — the writing is yours.
home.faq1A: Yes. Your narrative data is stored in a secure PostgreSQL database. Passwords are hashed and sensitive data is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM). No analytics or tracking tools are used.
home.faq2A: An interactive timeline, a relationship graph, a map of locations, the Save the Cat structure (15 beats), the Hero's Journey (12 stages), an emotional arc, an inconsistency detector, a setup-and-payoff tracker and subplot management.
home.faq3Q: Can I import an existing manuscript?
home.faq3A: Yes. Generate an analysis prompt with Atlas Narratif, send it to the AI of your choice (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude), then import the JSON result to automatically extract the timeline, characters and locations.
home.faq4Q: Does Atlas Narratif handle multi-volume series?
home.faq4A: Yes. Multi-volume support lets you filter by volume, track setups and payoffs from one book to the next, and visualise arcs across the whole series.

orphanChar.title: {{name}} doesn't appear in any event
orphanChar.explanation: The character "{{name}}" exists in the lore but is not linked to any timeline event.

orphanLoc.title: Location "{{name}}" is never visited
orphanLoc.explanation: The location "{{name}}" exists in the lore but is not linked to any timeline event.

brokenHolder.title: Unknown bearer for "{{name}}"
brokenHolder.explanation: The object "{{name}}" is assigned to "{{holder}}" but this character doesn't exist in the database.

brokenRef.title: Deleted entity still linked to events
brokenRef.explanation: An entity (id: {{entityId}}) is referenced in "{{eventTitle}}" but no longer exists in the lore.

deadReappear.title: {{name}} appears after their death ("{{deathEvent}}")
deadReappear.explanation: {{name}} is marked as dead in "{{deathEvent}}" (ch.{{deathChapter}}) but appears in: {{events}}.

inactiveObj.title: "{{name}}" used after being {{status}} (ch.{{chapter}})
inactiveObj.explanation: The object "{{name}}" is marked as {{status}} since chapter {{chapter}} but appears in: {{events}}.

payoffBeforePlant.title: Payoff of "{{label}}" precedes its setup
payoffBeforePlant.explanation: The setup "{{label}}" is placed at chapter {{plantChapter}} but its payoff is at chapter {{payoffChapter}}.

ghostAffil.title: Member not found in group "{{name}}"
ghostAffil.explanation: The group "{{name}}" references a character (id: {{charId}}) that no longer exists in the lore.

openPlant.title: Unresolved setup: "{{label}}"
openPlant.explanation: The setup "{{label}}" (placed ch.{{plantChapter}}) has no payoff defined while the story goes up to chapter {{maxChapter}}.

emptyThread.title: Thread "{{name}}" is not linked to any scene
emptyThread.explanation: The thread "{{name}}" exists but no timeline event is associated with it.

povMissing.title: POV character is missing from scene "{{title}}"
povMissing.explanation: The scene "{{title}}" (ch.{{chapter}}) has a POV character defined but this character is not listed among the scene's entities.

emptyScene.title: Scene with no entities or location: "{{title}}"
emptyScene.explanation: The event "{{title}}" (ch.{{chapter}}) is not linked to any character, location, or object.

crossDead.title: {{name}} dead in V{{volume}} reappears in a later volume
crossDead.explanation: {{name}} is marked as dead in "{{deathEvent}}" (V{{volume}}) but appears in: {{events}}.

crossObj.title: "{{name}}" {{status}} in V{{volume}} but used in a later volume
crossObj.explanation: The object "{{name}}" is marked as {{status}} (ch.{{chapter}}, V{{volume}}) but appears in: {{events}}.

crossPlant.title: Setup "{{label}}" with no payoff across the series
crossPlant.explanation: The setup "{{label}}" is placed in V{{volume}} but has no payoff defined across the entire series.

flashDeath.title: {{name}} in a flashback after their death (ch.{{chapter}})
flashDeath.explanation: {{name}} dies at chapter {{chapter}} but appears in flashbacks whose diegetic position is later: {{events}}.

flashObj.title: "{{name}}" in a flashback after being {{status}} (ch.{{chapter}})
flashObj.explanation: The object "{{name}}" is {{status}} since chapter {{chapter}} but appears in diegetically later flashbacks: {{events}}.

flashNoRef.title: Flashback without diegetic position: "{{title}}"
flashNoRef.explanation: The event "{{title}}" (ch.{{chapter}}) is marked as a flashback but has no defined diegetic position.

incDesc.Continuité de Personnage: A character marked as dead reappears in an event after their death.
incDesc.Continuité d'Objet: A lost or destroyed object is still used in scenes after its status change.
incDesc.Payoff Avant Plant: A narrative payoff is placed at an earlier chapter than its setup.
incDesc.Entité Non Référencée: A deleted lore entity is still referenced in timeline events.
incDesc.Incohérence de Porteur: The current bearer of an object doesn't match any known character.
incDesc.Affiliation Fantôme: A group references a member whose character was deleted from the lore.
incDesc.Personnage POV Absent: The POV character of a scene is not listed among its entities.
incDesc.Plant Sans Payoff: A narrative setup is marked as open with no payoff by the end of the story.
incDesc.Fil Narratif Vide: A narrative thread exists but no timeline event is associated with it.
incDesc.Entité Orpheline: A character or location exists in the lore but is never linked to a timeline event.
incDesc.Scène Vide: A timeline event is not linked to any entity (character, location, or object).
incDesc.Mort Cross-Tomes: A character who died in one volume reappears alive in a later volume.
incDesc.Objet Cross-Tomes: A lost or destroyed object from one volume is still used in a later volume.
incDesc.Plant Cross-Tomes: A setup from one volume has no payoff across the entire series.
incDesc.Flashback Temporel: A character or object appears in a flashback whose diegetic position is after their death or destruction.
incDesc.Flashback Non Ancré: A flashback has no defined diegetic position, making temporal coherence checks impossible.

missing.title: Undefined POV
missing.detail: {{count}} chapters with no POV character — the viewpoint stays unclear.

gap.title: Character eclipsed
gap.detail: {{name}} disappears for {{count}} chapters — is a return coming?

softBelly.title: Soft belly
softBelly.detail: {{count}} low-tension chapters in a row — readers may drift.

peaks.title: Peaks in a row
peaks.detail: {{count}} high-tension chapters with no respite — the intensity dulls.

flat.title: Flat curve
flat.detail: Intensity barely varies (std dev {{stdev}}) — the tension lacks relief.

noClimax.title: No real climax
noClimax.detail: No chapter passes {{threshold}}/10 (peak at {{max}}) — your dramatic high point is missing.

climaxEnd.title: Ending on the peak
climaxEnd.detail: Your last chapter is also your most intense — consider a wind-down scene after the climax.

climaxGood.title: Climax well placed
climaxGood.detail: Your intensity peak lands in the final third — good placement.

climaxEarly.title: Early climax
climaxEarly.detail: Your peak lands before the final third — the ending risks losing intensity.
